curation.lead:
Stewart Oldfield, CFA, CAIA, served as a Director at Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, Wealth Management, based at 345 Park Avenue in New York. From at least 2014 through 2019, he functioned as the primary relationship manager for the full constellation of Jeffrey Epstein’s accounts at Deutsche Bank — including Southern Trust Company, Southern Financial LLC, Gratitude America Ltd, the Haze Trust, and The 2017 Caterpillar Trust. His name surfaces with extraordinary density in the DOJ LMSBAND corpus: 1,818 co-occurrences with Richard Kahn (the single highest co-occurrence for Kahn) and 381 with Darren Indyke. These numbers place Oldfield at the operational center of the banking relationship that the New York Department of Financial Services would later fine Deutsche Bank $150 million for maintaining.

What makes Oldfield structurally significant is the dual-client arrangement. He simultaneously managed Epstein’s accounts and those of the Wanek family (Todd Wanek, Ashley Furniture heir) through Third Lake Capital, both filed under shared relationship manager codes RM 81851 and RM 82289. Internal Deutsche Bank pipeline spreadsheets list Southern Financial as a Tier 1 client and Third Lake Capital as Tier 2 — on the same document, under the same banker. Oldfield nominated both Epstein and Third Lake principals for the same Deutsche Bank-sponsored Frieze London art event, placing them on a shared invitation list. After departing Deutsche Bank, Oldfield became Principal and Chief Strategy Officer of Third Lake Partners LLC, the Wanek family office — an employer-to-client career transition that raises questions about the value he carried from the DB relationship.

Most critically, internal emails confirm Oldfield actively ran identity-concealment protocols for Epstein trust accounts. In a March 2019 email to Richard Kahn, Oldfield wrote: “There was no discussion of any names. Not even the name of the trust.” This was not passive negligence but deliberate operational security on behalf of a convicted sex offender whose identity Deutsche Bank’s own compliance function was supposedly monitoring. Oldfield was also directly CC’d on large cash withdrawal requests — including a January 2018 request for $100,000 in hundred-dollar bills, picked up by Darren Indyke under power of attorney.
open_questions: What were the circumstances and timing of Oldfield's departure from Deutsche Bank? Did he leave before or after the NYDFS investigation began, and was his departure negotiated as part of any internal remediation?

Did Oldfield participate in or provide testimony to the NYDFS investigation that resulted in the $150 million fine against Deutsche Bank for the Epstein relationship? His central role as RM makes him an indispensable witness.

What is the full scope of the Third Lake Partners relationship — did any Epstein-connected capital or entities flow into Wanek family investments, or was the overlap purely administrative? The shared RM codes create the structural possibility of cross-pollination.

How many total "Large Withdrawal" requests were there in the series? The January 2018 request was labeled "III," implying at least two prior large cash extractions that have not been fully documented.
What was the nature of the Marrakech property purchase for which Oldfield was asked to verify $30M+ in March 2019? Who was the buyer, and what entity held the funds?
Did Oldfield have any communication with Deutsche Bank compliance about the Epstein accounts, and if so, what did he represent about the client's identity and activities?
curation.system_role: Oldfield was the Deutsche Bank relationship manager who operationalized the bank's Epstein account retention, managing identity concealment, large cash withdrawals, and trust-level banking while simultaneously servicing the Wanek family accounts under shared RM codes — a dual portfolio that he parlayed into post-DB employment at the Wanek family office.

sections.title: Identity Concealment and Compliance Circumvention
sections.content:
The single most incriminating piece of evidence in the Oldfield dossier is his March 2019 email to Richard Kahn: “There was no discussion of any names. Not even the name of the trust. Thanks.” This message, sent from his Deutsche Bank email (stewart.oldfield@db.com), confirms that Oldfield was not merely aware of Epstein’s desire for anonymity — he was actively managing the concealment. When Deutsche Bank’s internal processes or counterparties might have surfaced the name of the trust’s beneficial owner, Oldfield ensured they did not.

This was not an isolated incident. In November 2016, Oldfield exchanged emails with Todd Stevens (Managing Director, Head of Key Client Partners - Americas) about how to structure Epstein’s ongoing relationship management. Stevens proposed getting “Shoshan to cover Jeffrey Epstein using his CA number,” and Oldfield responded: “That’s a great solution I think. We know JE likes syndicate. Will need Josh to be up to speed on the more interesting PE/HF offerings if and when we have them.” The exchange reveals a bank that treated Epstein not as a compliance liability but as a valued client requiring customized investment product access. Oldfield was the person translating that institutional posture into operational reality.

Oldfield also provided AML clearance letters to Mile Lukic at LGT Bank for Haze Trust verification in April 2019, managing the interbank compliance channel via SWIFT MT199. This placed him as the gatekeeper between Deutsche Bank’s internal compliance representations and external banking counterparties — the person certifying to other financial institutions that the accounts were clean.

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Oldfield’s network within the Epstein orbit was defined by three primary axes: the Epstein inner circle, Deutsche Bank management, and the Wanek family.

His deepest documented relationship was with Richard Kahn, Epstein’s financial manager and president of Gratitude America Ltd. The 1,818 LMSBAND co-occurrences between Oldfield and Kahn represent the single highest co-occurrence count for Kahn in the entire corpus, exceeding even Kahn’s co-occurrences with Darren Indyke. This reflects the reality that Kahn, not Epstein, was the day-to-day counterparty for banking operations, and Oldfield was the banker on the other side of every transaction. They communicated about Gratitude America, the Haze Trust, Rothschild investments, and compliance inquiries.

With Darren Indyke, Oldfield corresponded extensively about Prytanee LLC, CDD (Customer Due Diligence) forms, and account management (381 LMSBAND co-occurrences). Indyke served as the legal counterparty — the person with power of attorney who physically picked up large cash withdrawals and signed account documentation. Oldfield also had a direct personal meeting with Epstein himself on January 30, 2017 at Epstein’s East 71st Street residence. Kahn attended. That same day, Epstein’s calendar shows meetings with Boris Nikolic, Leon Black, and others — Oldfield was slotted into a day of high-value relationship management.

The Wanek relationship operated in parallel. Oldfield was named as the “Banker Team” lead for Third Lake Capital in Deutsche Bank’s Account Planning documents, managing over $100M in AUM with weekly contact. After leaving Deutsche Bank, he became Principal and CSO of Third Lake Partners — effectively converting a banking client into an employer.

sections.title: Financial Operations and Cash Withdrawals
sections.content:
Oldfield was directly CC’d on the “Epstein Large Withdrawal III” email chain in January 2018. The sequence began with Cynthia Rodriguez (Epstein’s assistant) requesting $100,000 in cash, preferably in hundred-dollar bills, with Darren Indyke designated as the authorized pickup person under his power of attorney over Epstein’s personal account. The Deutsche Bank branch could only assemble part of the amount in $100 bills, requiring the remainder in smaller denominations. The withdrawal was scheduled for January 17, 2018, and required documentation including government ID, residential address, date of birth, SSN, and account number. The fact that this was labeled “Large Withdrawal III” indicates it was at least the third such request in a pattern of large cash extractions.

Beyond cash withdrawals, Oldfield managed the broader financial architecture. Internal pipeline spreadsheets (EFTA01475567) show him assigned as the sales team member overseeing a diverse portfolio of high-net-worth clients: Parami Capital ($1.3M), ORIX ($10M+), the Lindemann family ($2.9M), and others. Within this portfolio, Southern Financial was classified as a Tier 1 client and Third Lake Capital as Tier 2, with products including $10M in real estate lending, PE fund allocations, and $5M in preferred CDs. The same spreadsheet that tracked ordinary wealth management clients tracked the Epstein entity constellation.

Oldfield was also involved in verifying $30M+ for a Marrakech property purchase in March 2019 and in closing accounts associated with Karyna Shuliak in April 2019 — the final months before Epstein’s arrest. The Carbyne investment was also channeled through Deutsche Bank, with Indyke referencing “the transferring bank which is DB” and directing Kahn to contact “Stew” — almost certainly Oldfield — to execute the wire.

sections.title: The Dual Portfolio: Epstein and Wanek Under Shared RM Codes
sections.content:
The most structurally unusual feature of Oldfield’s Deutsche Bank tenure is the co-mingling of the Epstein and Wanek relationships under shared relationship manager codes RM 81851 and RM 82289. Daily deposit reports under these codes captured ALL accounts in both portfolios, meaning that internally at Deutsche Bank, the Epstein entity constellation and the Wanek family office were managed as parts of a single banker’s book of business.

The overlap was not merely administrative. Oldfield discussed both client families in the same internal communications. One email (EFTA01383799) shows him wanting to “discuss DBNY sweep from brokerage accounts held at KCP (Southern Financial) and how to approach discussions about our promotional rate with Southern and Third Lake since they have so many different entities with accounts and so many assets here already.” Southern Financial was Epstein; Third Lake was Wanek. Oldfield was managing their promotional rate negotiations in the same breath.

The relationship extended to social events. A Deutsche Bank-sponsored Frieze London art event invitation list shows Oldfield nominating both Jeffrey Epstein for a “preview” and Ron Wanek/Ken Jones of Third Lake for “dinner and preview” — placing a convicted sex offender and a legitimate furniture magnate on the same curated guest list. The question this raises is whether the Wanek relationship provided institutional cover for retaining Epstein. A Tier 1 client (Southern Financial) bundled with a Tier 2 client (Third Lake) under the same RM codes meant that exiting Epstein would have risked disrupting the larger, more legitimate Wanek relationship.

After leaving Deutsche Bank, Oldfield became Principal and Chief Strategy Officer of Third Lake Partners LLC, confirmed by SEC Form D filings from 2022 onward. His career trajectory — Credit Suisse, Deutsche Bank, then the family office of his largest non-Epstein client — follows a pattern where the banker captured the client relationship as personal equity, converting a Deutsche Bank managed account into a direct employment arrangement.

sections.title: Trust Architecture and Entity Management
sections.content:
Oldfield was the Deutsche Bank point person for The 2017 Caterpillar Trust, one of the primary Epstein trust vehicles formed on January 3, 2017. He was named on bank statements from June 2018 onward and handled trustee matters and follow-ups. His in-person meeting with Epstein on January 30, 2017 — just weeks after the trust’s formation — suggests he was involved in the operational standup of the account. The follow-up email referencing “levered muni structures” indicates the trust was being used for leveraged municipal bond strategies, not merely as a passive holding vehicle.

Beyond the Caterpillar Trust, Oldfield’s fingerprints appear across the Epstein entity landscape. He managed the bank accounts for Gratitude America Ltd, Epstein’s ostensible philanthropy that in practice served as a disbursement vehicle for payments to figures like Landon Thomas Jr. and the International Peace Institute. He handled Haze Trust documentation and was involved in insurance trust paperwork. The entity known as BV 70 LLC also appears in his communications — the same vehicle through which Leon Black’s $10 million payment was routed through Gratitude America.

The breadth of Oldfield’s entity coverage means he had visibility into the full architecture of Epstein’s financial life at Deutsche Bank: the personal accounts, the trust accounts, the foundations, the LLCs, and the interbank transfers to institutions like LGT Bank. No single banker at Deutsche Bank appears to have had a more complete view of how the pieces fit together.
